$comment: Spec 120 §3.4 / Spec 122 §8 — the INTERPRETATION file for compute_maxbld_scenarios, capped at 12 prose entries (notes-cap.mjs).
MB-31 lane E stage 7 (plan section 5 Identity). Edits never improve a measured value: numbers are filled at the first run (MB-35).

read_this_way.what: A row is one field of one building type on one lot. Its `trace` is what the evaluator read, in read order (target, setting, fact, geometry, flag, upstream row, switch) — it is the audit trail for that one value, not a log of the run.

A row that gave up is `not_evaluated`, never a guessed number, and it propagates: every row that names it is `not_evaluated` with the same reason first seen (R3-01). `undecided` lists every input the row is waiting on, so a single missing Phase 2 cell explains a whole column.

The front-yard chain is the only place where a user number is mixed with a survey number: every non-user value carries a survey flag on the row (`front_yard_needs_survey` and friends, held in the catalogue, never in code), so a reader can tell which link of the chain is unchecked. The FS-SB2a ring placeholder is calibration provisional (L31-18).

S-1 and S-2 are logic variables with citations, not by-law numbers, and the S-1 storey count is flagged as a theoretical maximum (L31-14) — an S-1-derived value is the ceiling of the reading, not its typical value.

A box-shaped building footprint is an assumption: when the shape is not known the value is marked with the box flag, and the shape_calibration switch records that the box was assumed rather than the shape read (LC-69).
A re-run that writes zero rows is healthy: the runner's guarded upsert compares `content_sha` first, so an unchanged environment is a no-op write, and any write means something upstream moved.
Numeric values are not reproduced here. They are measured at the first real run (MB-35) and pasted back; an entry still reading `pending` has never been observed.

known_normal.what: `status` of `not_applicable` and `unlimited` are ordinary answers, not failures: the by-law says the field does not apply or does not cap it.

known_bad.what: A `reason` beginning `expression_error:` means the catalogue and the evaluator disagree (unknown target, unit mismatch) — a data or code defect, never a lot property.

limitations.what: `permitted` is provisional (M-417): the permission code is read as stored, not re-derived here.
The 15.0 m averaging radius is read from `l2(averaging_distance_m)` only once Phase 2 stores it (MB-18 (k)); until then the ring chain stays `not_evaluated`.
No clause switch is in use: `clause:<id>` is honoured when the switchboard declares it off, and today the switchboard declares none.
